newsitem.title: USA: Zapata urges Envirodyne to sell itself.
newsitem.headline: Zapata urges Envirodyne to sell itself.

text.p: Zapata Corp. said Friday it is recommending that Envirodyne Industries Inc., a Chicago-based packaging company, put itself up for sale and enlist the help of an investment banking firm.
Zapata said it made the proposal following an offer made by HK Acquisition Corp. on Thursday to buy Envirodyne's outstanding shares for $8.50 a share, or about $652 million.
HK Acquisitions was formed by Michael Heisley, a director of Envirodyne, and Donald Kelly, the company's former chairman.

Zapata is the largest minority stockholder of Envirodyne, with a 40 percent stake. In May, Zapata terminated its $8 a share proposal to acquire all of Envirodyne's common stock that it did not already own.

By hiring investment bankers and putting itself up for sale, Envirodyne would "level the playing field" for all possible bidders, Zapata said in a letter with the proposal, portions of which were released to the press.
"Under these circumstances, Zapata would give serious consideration to making a higher offer for Envirodyne," the company's letter said.
Zapata also said it has urged Envirodyne -- as part of any sales process -- to place into a separate liquidating trust the eventual proceeds from its recent $102 million patent infringement award.
Envirodyne's stock edged up 6 cents to 8.25 on Nasdaq in late trading. Zapata was unchanged at $4.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
